“Anthropic, the San Francisco company behind the Claude family of artificial intelligence models, has signed its first Australian data centre agreement, for the Western Downs Digital Park.

Premier David Crisafulli, described the $32 billion campus as the largest data centre proposed in Australia and a project that will position Queensland at the forefront of locking in data sovereignty.

The park is the work of Zerra DC, the data centre arm of Singapore-based AGP Sustainable Real Assets, which lodged its development application with Western Downs Regional Council on 17 August 2026. Anthropic has agreed to take the first of the four planned data halls, as reported by the ABC with the capacity to grow across the campus, and aims to begin using it in 2027.

Daily devotion 🙏🏻✝️☝️❤️‍🔥

Living in a World You Don’t

 Recognize

Have you ever looked up from your life and realized the predictable world you once counted on seems to have disappeared? 

Maybe it happened slowly. People you once trusted became a bit strange or unreliable. The news stopped making sense. A career that once felt secure started to feel fragile. 

You're not imagining it. The pace of change in our world is unlike anything we've experienced. Artificial intelligence alone is being called a disruption ten times bigger than the Industrial Revolution, and ten times faster. And even if you don't follow technology closely, you already feel the ripple effects — in your workplace, in your kids' lives, in the chatbot that takes your call instead of a real person, and in ordinary conversation that's become more polarized and less mutually encouraging. 

Psalm 46 has grounded generations of God's people. The Psalmist doesn't promise a calm world. Instead, he calls out to a steady God in a wildly unsteady world. 
God — not people, not work, not money, not predictability — is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear. 

Then the Psalmist drops this: we will not fear though the earth gives way. 
But how do you keep a sound mind when everything is changing? Amazon founder Jeff Bezos once said he deals with complexity not by focusing on what's going to change in the next ten years. Instead, he thinks about what won't change. 
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. And you can rest in that no matter how quickly the world or your world changes. 

CALL TO ACTION 

Write down one thing you know to be true about God that doesn't depend on your circumstances. Carry that with you today. 

PRAYER 

God, the world feels louder and more uncertain than it used to. I don't have all the answers, and honestly, I'm not sure I even know all the questions. But you are the same today as you have always been, and that is enough to take the next step. Be my anchor. Amen.
